Proves AR-6's `neq` operator on a `string` field: case-insensitive comparison by default (SEM-1) combined with SEM-2's null-handling rule — a negative operator MUST include NULL-valued rows in its match set, so the compiled predicate is never a bare inequality but `COLLATE craticula_ci <> $1 OR IS NULL` (and its Mongo/Search equivalents). Per SEM-1's pinned collation-vs-pattern-match split, the case-insensitive comparison uses a collation (Postgres `craticula_ci`, Mongo query-level `collation: {locale, strength: 2}`), never `ILIKE`/`$regex` — that pattern-match mechanism is reserved for `contains`/`notContains`/`startsWith`/`endsWith`.
